collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 35 or older and a young adult, 18-25)

collection.description: A villager who once failed as a healer meets a young apprentice who just failed: tell the story, or just sit together.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: When (subject) was young, (subject.he/she) tried to become a healer. (subject.He/she) was bad at it. Truly bad. (subject.He/she) fainted at the sight of a splinter. (subject.He/she) gave up and went into fishing instead, a little ashamed, and turned out to love it. Today, (friend), a young apprentice, has just failed at (friend.his/her) first craft and is sitting on the beach looking like the world has ended.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) doesn't say anything clever. (subject.He/she) just sits down and looks at the sea with (friend) for a while. After a long time, (friend) says, "Did you ever fail at something?" "Spectacularly," says (subject). "It was the best thing that ever happened to me. I didn't know that for years, though." (friend) thinks about that. It doesn't fix today. But it's something to remember.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) sits down and tells (friend.him/her) about the splinter and the fainting. (friend) laughs in spite of (friend.him/her)self. "And then?" "And then I found something I liked better. And I've been happy ever since. Mostly." (friend) isn't comforted right away. But (friend.he/she) asks (subject) to show (friend.him/her) how to mend a net. Just to see.
